name: agent-relay
label: Agent relay (structured)
lede: The same run, reached by another agent over a constrained vocabulary rather than by a person typing. Same engine, same rules, no free text.
_note: Hand-built demonstration payload. NOT engine output. Drawn only from the 8 erga already public in data/erga.json on main. Every absent[] reason below is a statement about that 8-ergon subset, not about the 171-ergon canon.

entry.assertion: Two E. coli strains (BL21(DE3) and K-12) and two Klebsiella species (K. pneumoniae and K. aerogenes KCTC 2190) account for 40.24% of all duodenal bacteria in SIBO subjects (≥10³ CFU/mL on MAC) vs 5.6% in non-SIBO subjects. Shotgun sequencing (n=38) confirmed these specific strains. The E. coli strains were hardly detectable in non-SIBO duodenum. Enterobacteriaceae RA was increased in SIBO subjects (log₂ FC 2.43, adjusted P=2.66E-7).
In IMO-positive subjects (CH4 >= 10 ppm), breath CH4 levels correlate with constipation severity (R=0.577, P=0.019).

returned.assertion: Twelve sugar pyruvate fermentation pathways and mixed acid fermentation are enriched in the duodenal microbiome of SIBO subjects (≥10³ CFU/mL on MAC) compared to non-SIBO (FC >1.1, adjusted P<.05). Aerobic cleavage of pyruvate is also enriched, including pyruvate to cytochrome bd/bo oxidase electron transfer (FC=1.48, adjusted P=2.09E-09). These pathways correlated with diarrhea (r=0.252, P=.0034), bloating (r=0.185, P=.025), urgency (r=0.205, P=.0146), and abdominal pain (r=0.300, P=.0006). Enterobacteriaceae species produce H₂ from sugar fermentation, and microbial reactions known to produce or consume H₂ are largely represented by pyruvate fermentation coupled with aerobic/anaerobic respiration.

Assimilatory sulfate reduction pathways (I, III, and IV) are enriched in the duodenal microbiome of SIBO subjects (≥10³ CFU/mL on MAC) compared to non-SIBO subjects. Pathway enrichment FCs: 1.541 (P=8.25E-10), 1.6575 (P=2.87E-11), and 1.115 (P=.020825). Sulfate assimilation and cysteine biosynthesis superpathway also enriched (FC 1.14, P=1.00E-07). Assimilatory pathways I and III correlated with diarrhea severity (Spearman r=0.193, P=.031 and r=0.190, P=.033 respectively).

Supplementation with 21 g/d of poorly digested soluble fibers (polydextrose or soluble corn fiber) for 21 days shifted the fecal Bacteroidetes:Firmicutes ratio in healthy men (n=21, crossover RCT). Firmicutes decreased from 68% (no-fiber control) to 56% (polydextrose) and 55% (SCF) (P<0.001). Bacteroidetes increased from 25% to 36% and 38% respectively (P<0.001). The B:F ratio correlated positively with total dietary fiber intake (r=0.45, P=0.003) but NOT with BMI (r=0.06, P=0.64). Parabacteroides was the primary driver, increasing 4-5× (1.66%→6.83% PDX, 7.94% SCF, P<0.001). However, known butyrate producers Eubacterium (11.2%→6.31% PDX, 5.94% SCF), Dorea (1.32%→0.81% PDX, 0.82% SCF), and Roseburia (3.80%→2.33% PDX, 2.40% SCF) all DECREASED with fiber (P<0.001). Butanoate metabolism genes were depleted 15-20% (P=0.001, q=0.004). Amino acid metabolism genes showed the largest functional enrichment after fiber (P<0.0001).

absent.reason: Nothing in this subset connects a named organism to a dietary intervention. The nutrition ergon here is indexed by what was fed, not by what was living there — so an entry that arrives naming organisms cannot reach it directly.
